claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT calculations can identify a ferromagnetic ground state.
Spin-polarized DFT captures exchange interactions relevant to magnetic ordering.
Exchange interactions can lower the total energy of a spin-aligned configuration relative to other magnetic orderings.
The proposed method compares total energies of ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and non-magnetic configurations using spin-polarized DFT.
GGA or LDA+U may be suitable exchange-correlation treatments for this calculation.
The calculations are to represent zero-temperature equilibrium conditions.
Crystal structure and the resulting electronic band structure mediate exchange interactions between magnetic ions.
DFT accounts for electron exchange and correlation effects.
A ferromagnetic state with a lower computed total energy than non-magnetic and antiferromagnetic states indicates that exchange splitting favors ferromagnetic ordering.
The ferromagnetic configuration is predicted to have a lower computed total energy than alternative spin arrangements.
A lower computed energy for the ferromagnetic configuration confirms a ferromagnetic ground state within the configurations and computational model considered.
The non-magnetic and antiferromagnetic energies computed under the same DFT framework provide comparison baselines.
The predictive power of the calculation is limited by the accuracy of the selected exchange-correlation functional.
The proposed calculation may not fully capture strong electron-correlation effects.
A zero-temperature DFT comparison may not fully account for temperature-dependent magnetic fluctuations.
The calculated energy difference and predicted ordering depend on functional choice and material-specific characteristics.
Magnetic moments and electronic density of states showing exchange splitting are proposed as supplementary measurements.
Failure of the ferromagnetic configuration to have the lowest calculated energy is stated to falsify the reliability of spin-polarized DFT for indicating a ferromagnetic ground state.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis presents energy comparison as a method for determining whether the ground state is ferromagnetic, whereas the falsification rule treats a non-ferromagnetic lowest-energy result as falsifying the method itself. Such a result would ordinarily reject the material-specific ferromagnetic-ground-state prediction within the model, not the general ability of DFT to compare magnetic states.
